name: Fused Mandibular Incisors

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiographic Diagnostic Criteria for Dental Fusion

criteria.description: Presence of clinically fused mandibular incisors with joined crowns
Radiographic evidence of conjoined dentin and/or pulp chambers between mandibular incisors
Exclusion of gemination and other dental anomalies through clinical and radiographic assessment
No associated syndromic features or systemic conditions

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Clinical evidence of fused mandibular incisors with radiographic confirmation of joined dentin or pulp chambers, excluding other dental anomalies
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Differentiation from gemination is critical; fusion involves two separate tooth buds, whereas gemination involves a single tooth bud.

pathognomonic.notes: Visible union of two adjacent mandibular incisor crowns

imaging: Radiographic evidence of fused dentin and pulp chambers in mandibular incisors
Panoramic and periapical dental X-rays showing conjoined tooth structures
genetic: No specific genetic mutations identified; generally considered a developmental anomaly
other: Clinical examination revealing joined crowns of mandibular incisors
Differentiation from gemination and concrescence by clinical and radiographic assessment

distinguishingFeatures: Single enlarged tooth with bifid crown
Single root and root canal system
No fusion of two separate tooth buds
Union of teeth by cementum only
No fusion of dentin or pulp chambers

redFlags: Rapid progression of dental caries in fused teeth
Development of dental abscess or facial swelling
Severe malocclusion impacting mastication or speech
